chunk_findings.detail: `action='count'` is a standard, repeatable argparse action: `parser.add_argument('-v', '--verbose', action='count')` accepts `-v -v -v` and accumulates the value. But `_repeats` returns False for `argparse._CountAction` because it is not `_AppendAction`/`_ExtendAction` and its module is `"argparse"` with `nargs == 0`. So `command_tree(parser)['options'][0]['repeat']` is False, telling the completion consumer the flag cannot be given again when it can.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion/tree.py:_repeats

chunk_findings.detail: `_parsers` treats every entry in `a.choices.items()` as a canonical command path, but the completion tree intentionally omits aliases and hidden commands. The file’s own `_compat_parser` proves the mismatch: it adds `aliases=("display",)`, and line 79 asserts `"display" in sub.choices`, while `got["commands"] == ["show"]`. Given that parser, `_parsers` yields both `("show",)` and `("display",)`, but `T.walk` omits `("display",)`, so the exact equality `set(walked) == set(paths)` would fail. The same false failure occurs for `build_parser()` as soon as it contains any command alias or hidden subcommand, which makes this “nothing missing, nothing extra” assertion incompatible with the alias-hiding behavior the test suite is meant to enforce.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_completion_tree.py:32-39

chunk_findings.detail: `from ddflow.services.completion import *` is broken by the module-to-package conversion. `import *` does not consult module `__getattr__` for each public name; it uses the package's own `__dict__` (and `__all__` if defined, but it is not). A client that previously did `from ddflow.services.completion import *` and then called `verdict(...)` now imports only `Any` and `import_module` from this `__init__.py`, so it fails at the call with `NameError: name 'verdict' is not defined`. To preserve the old namespace, `__init__.py` must define `__all__` from `.rules` or otherwise re-export the star-import names.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion/__init__.py:__getattr__

chunk_findings.detail: `parser.add_argument('--tag', action='append_const', const='x')` and `parser.add_argument('-v', action='count')` create `argparse._AppendConstAction` and `argparse._CountAction`, both of which argparse allows to repeat (`--tag --tag`, `-v -v`) and accumulates/increments. `_repeats` only recognizes `argparse._AppendAction` and `argparse._ExtendAction`; for both of these stock argparse actions it returns `False`, so the tree reports `"repeat": False`, misleading downstream completion logic.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion/tree.py:_repeats

chunk_findings.detail: For `parser.add_argument('rest', nargs=argparse.REMAINDER)`, `argparse.REMAINDER` is `'...'`, so `_arity` returns `'...'` via `str(a.nargs)`. The function’s own documented return vocabulary is `0`, `1`, `?`, `*`, `+`, or an integer as text; `'...'` is none of these, so a valid argparse parser produces an arity token downstream completion clients following that contract cannot interpret.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion/tree.py:_arity

chunk_findings.detail: `_parsers` iterates every entry in `a.choices.items()` and does not filter hidden/deprecated command aliases, even though the tree is explicitly required to omit them. The same file demonstrates the conflict: `_compat_parser()` adds `"display"` as an alias, `test_compat_flags_and_command_aliases_are_not_offered` asserts `"display" in sub.choices` but also `list(got["commands"]) == ["show"]`, so `T.walk` must not yield `("display",)`. Applying the `test_every_path_matches_argparse` comparison to `_compat_parser()` (or any real parser with a hidden alias) makes `paths` contain `("display",)` while `walked` does not, so `assert set(walked) == set(paths)` fails even though the tree is correct. `test_real_parser_compat_names_are_not_offered` would also crash because `T.at(tree, hidden_path)` returns `None` and then `node["options"]` raises `TypeError`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_completion_tree.py _parsers / test_every_path_matches_argparse

chunk_findings.detail: The added assertion `assert "display" not in dict(sub.choices.items())` is false under the test’s own parser: `argparse._SubParsersAction.choices` is the name→parser map and `add_parser("show", aliases=("display",))` inserts `"display"` into it, so `sub.choices.items()` contains `("display", ...)`. This is contradicted by the immediately preceding assertion `assert "display" in sub.choices`, and the sampled input (`ArgumentParser`, `add_subparsers()`, `add_parser("show", aliases=("display",))`) raises `AssertionError`. Thus the previous finding still holds: `_parsers`, which walks `a.choices.items()`, still sees the alias while the completion tree omits it; the new assertion does not refute that mismatch and itself fails.
